cell_type.evidence: In this study, we investigated whether it is possible to assess the functional state of cancer-associated fibroblasts through tumor tissue proteome profiling.
Data were interpreted referring to reference proteome profiles generated from primary human mammary fibroblasts comprising 4095 proteins.
Representative for cancer cells, we investigated the mammary carcinoma cell line ZR-75-1, identifying 5212 proteins.

disease_state.evidence: Breast cancer is still the most common type of cancer in women; an important role in carcinogenesis is actually attributed to cancer-associated fibroblasts.
Tissue proteomics was performed on tumor-central, tumor-near, and tumor-distant biopsy sections from breast adenocarcinoma patients, which allowed us to identify 2074 proteins.

sample_source.evidence: Tumor-distant tissue sections from breast cancer biopsies homogenized with a glass glass homogenizer; isolation of the cytoplasmic protein fraction; SDS-PAGE separation of proteins; in gel digest of eight slices with trypsin including reduction of cysteins with DTT and alkylation with IAA; separation of peptides with nano-LC (Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano) using a 2cm C-18 trapping column with 100µm diameter and 5µm particle size and a 15cm C-18 separation column with 75µm diameter and 2µm particle size; peptides were eluted with a flow rate of 300nl/min from the pre-column to the analytical column and separated with a gradient of 1% to 40% mobile phase B (20% H2O, 80% ACN, 0.2% FA) over 45min; identification of peptides using a Thermo QExactive orbitrap mass spectrometer at a resolution of 40 000 (at m/z=200) for MS1 followed by MS/MS scans of the six most abundant ions upon fragmentation in the HCD cell at 30% normalized collision energy (isolation width of Δm/z = 2, resolution 17500 at m/z = 200).
